text: {"version":1,"kind":"conversation","reading":"The user is asking for a subjective recommendation, not a new data query, about which of the previously ranked players to build a team around.","measures":[],"groupBy":[],"display":[],"filters":[],"expectedShape":"scalar","unresolved":[],"provenance":{},"reply":"That's a judgment call rather than something the data alone can decide, but here's what the numbers from the 2017 ranking suggest: James Harden leads in points per game (30.08) and total points (2888) with strong assist support (9.79 apg), making him the top pure scorer/playmaker. Russell Westbrook is the most well-rounded, averaging a near triple-double (29.03 pts, 10.14 reb, 10.02 ast) — his rebounding and playmaking add value beyond scoring. LeBron James (28.20 pts, 8.76 reb, 8.70 ast) is the most balanced across all three categories with the fewest trade-offs. If you want a primary scorer, Harden; if you want an all-around floor general who impacts every stat category, Westbrook; if you want the steadiest all-around contributor, LeBron. Let me know if you'd like me to pull additional stats (shooting efficiency, turnovers, team wins) to make this comparison more rigorous."}
